text: Thou sayest not well, if thou thinkest that a man who is good for anything at all ought to compute the hazard of life or death, and should not rather look to this only in all that he does, whether he is doing what is just or unjust, and the works of a good or bad man.
author: Marcus Aurelius
speaker: Socrates (quoted from Plato)
location: On campaign on the Danube frontier, e.g. Carnuntum or Sirmium (presumed)
